docs.title: Presentation
docs.text:
OpenPlatform is the open-source project of the Firefly Software Foundation and Firefly Software Solutions Inc. They stay two bodies. The Foundation stewards the project. The company stands behind it. Contact remains the Firefly Software Foundation, dev@fireflysoftware.io.

It is a set of corporate systems for enterprise industries. Banking and insurance come first. Another industry can use the same shape later: a journey a person follows, a domain port that does one job, and a core that stores the rows. The institution runs the software. The data stays in the cores. A process engine, a payment rail, a card provider, or an identity service replaces an adapter. The journey does not change when that adapter changes.

Jafly is the framework the services are built with. It is the Java framework from Firefly Framework. OpenPlatform does not ship a second copy of it. The published documentation is version 26.10.4.

docs.title: One afternoon with Ada
docs.text:
The person in every chapter is Ada Lovelace. She signs in as sample-journey. That name resolves to actor 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111. She may read and create the sample resources. The username denied-actor is refused, and a refused caller never reaches a record.

The agreement that follows her is 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000021. The document that prints it is a Horizon Personal Loan, five years, two lines. That page is a reading copy. It is not a movement of money. Source: the sandbox sample prints 250,000.00 EUR.

What she sees first is her actor id and the provider name sandbox. No password is read, and no identity-provider process starts.

If she is new and names insurance, onboarding opens a contract and does not start an identity case. Insurance is not a regulated banking family. If she names deposits, cards, lending, or payments, onboarding registers her and waits for identity evidence. That split is onboarding.

Once she exists, profile lists the agreements the contract service holds for her. When agreement ...021 is among them, she sees its number, its status, and the product name Horizon Personal Loan.

If she sends money, that is payments. A domestic or international credit is reserved, she receives a numeric code, and only that code posts the ledger and then sends the rail. The word sandbox is not the code. An internal move, including a move between spaces of one account, posts the ledger and does not ask for a code. Money arriving from outside is accepted once and posted once. Cancel, while the money is only reserved, releases the hold.

If she wants cover, that is insurance. She asks for a quote, binds a policy, and registers a claim. Later she can change a status, withdraw the quote, cancel the policy, or close the claim. Endorse and renew are not on that journey. Insurance does not move money and does not certify IFRS 17 or Solvency II.

If she asks for the Horizon Personal Loan, that is lending. The product chooses the record. After the loan exists she can read the amortization calendar and, when the loan is syndicated, the facility. She can change the rate, close the loan, or take a payment holiday. Paying the money out tries, then confirms.

An employee who acts for her uses the finance terminal or the insurance terminal. Those desks are not her journey. They require administer, and a change in her name stores the employee id and her party id before the record changes.

docs.title: Where the records go
docs.text: A person row lives in the customer core. An agreement lives in the contract core. An account lives in the accounts core, and its opening entry is a ledger posting. A card lives in the cards core. A loan lives in the lending cores the product route names. A policy, a claim, and a quote live in the insurance cores. A printed contract is HTML in the document store. Money the bank holds is posted on core-banking-ledger, and only when a payment is confirmed.

docs.title: Jafly
docs.text:
Stewarded by the Firefly Software Foundation. dev@fireflysoftware.io

Jafly is the Java framework in Firefly Framework. The Firefly Software Foundation maintains the frameworks. Firefly Software Solutions Inc. builds services on them. They stay two bodies. OpenPlatform does not ship a second copy of Jafly, and it does not fork the rules engine or the identity adapters.

On the framework site, Jafly is the layer between Spring Boot and the business rules. Requests stay on Spring Boot and WebFlux. A service adds the modules it needs: command and query buses, orchestration for compensating steps and for try-confirm-cancel, reactive transactions, and observability. The framework release described there uses Java 25 and Spring Boot 4.1.1. The team still owns the business rules, who may act, and what a failed step undoes. The framework does not make a command exactly once.

OpenPlatform 26.10.4 sits on that foundation. firefly-parent 26.10.4 extends org.fireflyframework:fireflyframework-parent 26.10.20 and imports org.fireflyframework:fireflyframework-bom 26.10.20. Every OpenPlatform module inherits that pin. The module guide is at fireflyframework.org/frameworks/java.

docs.title: What Ada meets
docs.text:
Ada never calls Jafly by name. She signs in, and she sometimes waits for a decision. Both of those happen in OpenPlatform services that use Jafly underneath.

Sign-in is the security center, port 8085. With the identity adapter left at sandbox, the name sample-journey returns actor 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111 and provider sandbox. The password is ignored. Keycloak, Cognito, and an internal user store do not start. An installer sets firefly.security-center.identity.adapter to keycloak, cognito, or internal-db. Those three are Jafly identity adapters. The journey still does not open an identity-provider client. The security center selects the provider.

A decision is the credit-scoring service, port 8042. Ada's journey does not send a score. The sandbox report supplies 640 and says she is not high risk. The sample rules file is named openplatform-journey. Its threshold is 680. She sees REFER and CREDIT_SCORE_BELOW_THRESHOLD. A referral does not stop her. If the request says high risk, she sees DECLINE and HIGH_RISK, and the journey does not write the record. An installer replaces the rules file, or points firefly.decision.rulesets-directory at a directory of files. The installer does not replace the engine that reads the file.

Payments use the same foundation for a different pause. Try reserves the money. Confirm is a later call, after she returns the numeric code. The word sandbox is not that code. The payments chapter tells that story.

docs.title: What a refusal means for her
docs.text:
An unknown username is not a subject. She sees HTTP 404. A body with neither username nor actor id is HTTP 400. Nothing is written.

A decline stops the journey before the domain write. She does not get a party, a quote, a policy, a claim, or a loan application from that call. A referral is not a refusal. She continues, and the record is stored.

If an installer has selected a live identity provider and that process is not running, sign-in fails in that provider. The sandbox setting does not require it.

docs.title: Where this is stored
docs.text: The sandbox identity answer is not a row in an identity-provider database. The decision outcome is the rules file plus the report. The business record, when the outcome is not a decline, is written by the journey's own domain into that domain's core. Jafly does not own those tables.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
Stewarded by the Firefly Software Foundation. dev@fireflysoftware.io

This is one path through the sandbox, for OpenPlatform 26.10.4. The person is Ada Lovelace the whole way. You sign her in, you ask whether she may act, and you ask for a decision only when the step creates a record. The sandbox does not start an identity provider and it does not call a credit bureau. Jafly supplies the rules and the identity adapters. Their versions come from framework parent 26.10.20, imported by firefly-parent 26.10.4.

Her username is sample-journey. Her actor id is 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111. The agreement you will see printed, and the agreement a payment or a policy can name, is 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000021. The product on that agreement is the Horizon Personal Loan, 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000202.

docs.title: Who is calling
docs.text:
POST http://localhost:8085/api/v1/identity/subjects

{ "username": "sample-journey" }

She sees HTTP 200, actor 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111, and provider sandbox. An unknown username is HTTP 404. A body with neither a username nor an actor id is HTTP 400. The sandbox does not read a password. denied-actor, actor 22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222, can be resolved and then fails the next check.

docs.title: Whether she may create a party
docs.text:
POST http://localhost:8085/api/v1/access/checks

{
  // actorId: 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111
  // action: CREATE
  // resourceType: PARTY
  // resourceId: 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001
}

Both allow and deny return HTTP 200. She sees allowed: true and may continue. allowed: false means stop. Do not call the domain. That is what denied-actor sees.

docs.title: The decision, when the step creates a record
docs.text:
POST http://localhost:8042/api/v1/decisions

{
  // partyId: 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111
  // journeyStep: ONBOARDING
  // attributes: { highRisk: false }
}

Omit the score. The sandbox report fills 640. She sees REFER and CREDIT_SCORE_BELOW_THRESHOLD, because 640 is below 680. A referral does not stop her. highRisk: true is DECLINE and HIGH_RISK, and a decline does not write the record. The same call is used for INSURANCE_QUOTE, INSURANCE_BIND, CLAIM, and a lending application.

docs.title: The rest of the afternoon
docs.text:
Onboard her at POST http://localhost:8096/api/v1/onboarding/individuals. Send productFamily INSURANCE and she sees phase NON_REGULATED and a new contract id. She does not see an identity case. Send DEPOSITS, or omit the family, and she is registered and the journey waits for personal data, economic data, identity documents, a verification signal, and completion. The body is on onboarding.

Read what she holds at GET http://localhost:8103/api/v1/experience/profile/11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111/contracts. Each row is an agreement and the product on it. Agreement ...021 appears only when the contract service holds it for her. See profile.

Issue the reading copy of that agreement as template contract. She can read HTML: Horizon Personal Loan, five years, two lines, each part its own sheet. Source: the sandbox sample prints 250,000.00 EUR. See documents.

Send money from payments. Try, then confirm with the numeric code. The word sandbox does not confirm. The ledger posts on confirm, not on try. Cancel releases a hold that was never posted. An inbound credit posts once.

Quote, bind, and claim from insurance. Those three ask for a decision. Status, withdraw, cancel, and close do not. Insurance does not move the loan amount and does not post a ledger entry.

Apply for the Horizon Personal Loan at POST http://localhost:8102/api/v1/experience/lending/applications with product 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000202, the sample amount, and term 60. The journey reads journey.lending.min-credit-score before it decides. After the loan exists she can read GET /api/v1/experience/lending/loans/{id}/calendar. See lending.

docs.text:
Username Actor id What the sandbox allows sample-journey 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111 Read and create on the sample party, account, card, policy, claim, contract, and product. sample-employee 33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333 Read, plus administer and impersonate. denied-actor 22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222 Nothing. The access check returns allowed: false.

The employee does not use Ada's calls. The finance terminal is port 8120 and the insurance terminal is port 8121.

docs.title: Replace an adapter
docs.text:
Stewarded by the Firefly Software Foundation. dev@fireflysoftware.io

An installer does not rewrite Ada's journey to point at a new bank system. The journey calls a port. The port is a promise: hold this money, send this credit, say who this person is, evaluate this rules file, render this document. Which system keeps the promise is a property. One answer per port per deployment. The sandbox answer ships in the repository and does not open a network connection. The live answer is selected by configuration. Secrets stay out of the repository.

Ada's calls stay the same either way. She still signs in as sample-journey, tries a payment on agreement 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000021, or asks for a quote. What changes is who posts the ledger, who sends the rail message, and who says she is signed in. She should not have to learn the new system.

docs.title: What she still sees
docs.text: With every property left at the sandbox, a payment try returns a payment id and, for an outbound transfer, a numeric code. Confirm with that code posts in the sandbox book. The word sandbox is not the code. Sign-in still returns actor 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111. A decision that omits the score still sees 640 and, against the sample threshold 680, a referral. A document issue still returns HTML for the Horizon Personal Loan.

docs.title: Payments
docs.text:
firefly.payments.mode defaults to sandbox. The ledger hold and the later posting stay in memory. The rail and the card provider accept the instruction locally and do not send it. The numeric challenge is created by a stand-in for the strong-authentication core.

Set firefly.payments.mode to live and the same try and confirm post through core-banking-ledger. A credit transfer goes out through library-rails. International is SWIFT. A domestic transfer is SEPA when the catalog contains SEPA credit transfer. A card goes through library-psps. The challenge is created by core-common-sca-mgmt. Delivery of that code, in the wiring shipped here, still returns the code on the try response and does not send SMS, push, or email. An installer replaces that delivery.

firefly.payments.configuration defaults to sandbox. Set it to live when the routes, limits, currencies, and clearing accounts should be read from configuration and reference data instead of the sandbox lists.

docs.title: Identity, access, and the decision
docs.text:
firefly.security-center.identity.adapter defaults to sandbox. sample-journey is Ada. Set keycloak, cognito, or internal-db to use the matching Jafly provider. The journey does not construct that client.

firefly.security-center.access.adapter defaults to sandbox and reads sandbox-access-policy.json. Set session-grants when the check should use the role scopes on the party session. Replace the policy file to change who the sandbox allows. Do not hard-code allow and deny in a controller. denied-actor stays refused until that file grants him something.

firefly.decision.credit-report defaults to sandbox and returns score 640, not high risk, for every party. Any other value selects the report adapter the installer registers. The sandbox does not call a bureau.

firefly.decision.ruleset defaults to openplatform-journey. firefly.decision.rulesets-directory points at a directory of {name}.yaml files. Replacing the file changes approve, refer, and decline. It does not replace the engine.

docs.title: Catalog, documents, and the loan price
docs.text:
firefly.reference-data.catalog.adapter left unset uses the sandbox catalog. Deposits, payments, lending, and cards are regulated. Insurance is not. The document types are contract, amendment, renewal, letter, and welcome. Set the property to core to read reference data instead.

firefly.documents.storage defaults to the sandbox store. Set core to write the HTML, including the inlined kit stylesheet, into the document core.

firefly.lending.price.adapter, firefly.lending.ledger.adapter, and firefly.lending.accounting.adapter default to sandbox. The loan rate then comes from the product pricing configuration in that sandbox, the cash posting stays in memory, and the end-of-day journal stays in memory. Set them to the live values when the price, the ledger, and the general ledger should be the real services.

firefly.experience.payments.adapter defaults to sandbox for a loan disbursement. Set it to hub to try and confirm through the domain payments SDK. firefly.terminal.adapter defaults to the in-memory configuration. Set it to domain when a staff terminal should write through the domain services.

docs.title: What a refusal means
docs.text:
An unset property is the sandbox, not a failure. A live property with no address, or a provider process that is not running, fails the call that needs that system. The journey does not switch itself back to the sandbox. Ada sees the failure of that call. She does not see a silent fallback.

A rules file that is missing, or a catalog row that is missing, fails the decision or the document before the write. An international credit configured onto a card route is rejected. The rail is the path for that transfer.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
Port Sandbox until the property changes Property Ledger, rail, card provider, challenge creation In-process stand-ins firefly.payments.mode=live Challenge delivery Returns the code, sends no message Replace the delivery adapter Routes and masters Sandbox lists firefly.payments.configuration=live Identity sample-journey is Ada firefly.security-center.identity.adapter Access Policy file firefly.security-center.access.adapter Credit report Score 640 firefly.decision.credit-report Rules openplatform-journey.yaml firefly.decision.ruleset Catalog Sandbox families and document types firefly.reference-data.catalog.adapter=core Document store In-process HTML firefly.documents.storage=core Loan price, cash, and the day journal In-process firefly.lending.price.adapter, firefly.lending.ledger.adapter, firefly.lending.accounting.adapter

The type names are the port interfaces behind those properties. They are the footnote. Ada's paths do not change.

docs.title: How to read a call
docs.text:
A journey call is identity, then access, then a decision only when the operation creates a new risk, then the record. A refusal at access or a decline at the decision does not write that record.

Read an operation in this order. First the plain explanation of who calls it and what they get. Then the commented example, which is the body the service accepts. Then the Swagger panel. The panel is the OpenAPI file shipped with that service, copied to docs/api/specs/<journey>/openapi.yml. It is not typed by hand from a running process. Where the file names a path and a status but does not list every field, the example above the panel is the body the service reads.

The published version is 26.10.4.

Payments have no OpenAPI file. Try, confirm, and cancel are written on the payments page, with the commented example there.

docs.title: Insurance
docs.text:
Ada asks for cover, then binds it, then reports a loss. The three creates ask for a decision. A decline stores nothing. Status, withdraw, cancel, and close do not ask for a decision. Insurance does not move money.

She is sample-journey, party 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111. The policy can name sandbox agreement 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000021. That identifier is not a ledger posting. Omit the status and the catalog stores a quote as received, a policy as bound, and a claim as notified.

The service listens on port 8108. If access is not allowed, the call stops before the domain. A decline is the sample high-risk result. An operation switched off in the catalog is HTTP 409.

// POST /api/v1/experience/insurance/quotes
// Creates a submission. Decision runs. Default status RECEIVED.
{
  // tenantId: identifier, optional
  // partyId: 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111
  // productId: the cover
  // submissionNumber: optional business number
  // lineOfBusiness: MOTOR
  // submissionStatus: omit to use RECEIVED
  // currency: EUR
}
// 201
{
  // id: the submission
  // reference: business number
  // status: RECEIVED
}

// POST /api/v1/experience/insurance/policies
// Binds a policy. Decision runs. Default status BOUND.
{
  // partyId: 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111
  // contractId: 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000021
  // productId: the cover
  // lineOfBusiness: MOTOR
  // currency: EUR
  // inceptionDate: 2026-11-01
  // expiryDate: 2027-11-01
  // policyStatus: omit to use BOUND
}
// 201. id, reference, status BOUND

// POST /api/v1/experience/insurance/policies/{policyId}/cancel
{ "reason": "why she cancels" }
// 200. No decision.

// POST /api/v1/experience/insurance/claims
{
  // policyId: the bound policy
  // claimNumber: optional
  // lossDate: 2026-12-01
  // causeCode: the cause
  // description: what happened
  // currency: EUR
  // claimStatus: omit to use NOTIFIED
}
// 201

// POST /api/v1/experience/insurance/claims/{claimId}/close
{ "reason": "why it closes" }
// 200. No decision.

docs.title: Lending
docs.text:
Ada applies for credit. Access is checked first. The journey reads journey.lending.min-credit-score and sends that number with the decision. In the sandbox the parameter is 680. A decline stores nothing. The product id chooses the domain: personal loan, mortgage, asset finance, supply-chain finance, or, when the product is not listed, loan origination.

Product 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000202 is the Horizon Personal Loan. She can ask for that amount over 60 months, which is the five-year sample on agreement 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000021. Source: the sandbox sample is 250,000.00 EUR.

After the loan exists she can change the rate, close it, and take or end a payment holiday. Those do not move money. Disbursement and an installment payment try, then confirm, through the payments port. The sandbox is the default and does not post the ledger. firefly.experience.payments.adapter=hub uses the domain payments SDK. The word sandbox is not a valid code on that adapter.

A syndicated facility, when she reads one, returns the facility id, the loan id, the currency, the commitment, and the status. The participant register is not on that response. There is no separate syndicated-loan experience.

The service listens on port 8102. If access is not allowed, nothing is written. A decline stops before the domain. An operation the catalog has switched off is HTTP 409.

// POST /api/v1/experience/lending/applications
{
  // partyId: 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111
  // productId: 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000202
  // requestedAmount: 250000.00
  // term: 60
  // purpose: optional
}

// POST /api/v1/experience/lending/loans/{loanId}/rate
{
  // oldInterestRate
  // newInterestRate
  // effectiveDate
  // reason: INDEX_ADJUSTMENT, RENEGOTIATION, PENALTY, or PROMOTION
}

// POST /api/v1/experience/lending/loans/{loanId}/close
{ "reason": "why" }

// POST /api/v1/experience/lending/loans/{loanId}/payment-holiday
{ "reason": "why the holiday starts" }

// POST /api/v1/experience/lending/loans/{loanId}/payment-holiday/end
{ "reason": "why the holiday ends" }

// POST /api/v1/experience/lending/loans/{loanId}/disbursements
{ "amount": 250000.00 }
// try, then confirm, on the payments port

// POST /api/v1/experience/lending/loans/{loanId}/installments/{installmentId}/payments
{ "amount": the installment }

// GET /api/v1/experience/lending/loans/{loanId}/syndicated-facility
{
  // facilityId, loanId, currency, commitmentAmount, status
}

docs.title: Onboarding
docs.text:
A person or a company becomes a customer. Access is checked first. A decision follows. A decline writes nothing. The product family then chooses the path. INSURANCE opens a contract and does not start identity checks. DEPOSITS, PAYMENTS, LENDING, CARDS, or an omitted family registers the person and waits for the later signals.

Ada can send party 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111 so the decision is about her. The new contract from an insurance start is not agreement 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000021. That agreement is the sandbox Horizon Personal Loan. This call asks the contract service for a new id.

The service listens on port 8096. Denied access does not start. A decline does not register her. The published spec requires tenant, first name, last name, and email. The service also reads productFamily, partyId, and actorId when they are present.

// POST /api/v1/onboarding/individuals
// header X-Idempotency-Key: optional
{
  // tenantId: required
  // firstName: Ada
  // lastName: Lovelace
  // email: her email, required
  // phone: optional
  // nationalIdNumber: optional
  // dueDiligenceLevel: STANDARD when omitted
  // partyId: 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111
  // actorId: defaults to the party id
  // productFamily: INSURANCE or DEPOSITS
}
// Insurance response
{
  // onboardingId: the new contract id
  // partyId: the party sent above
  // currentPhase: NON_REGULATED
  // nextStep: INSURANCE
}
// Deposit response waits for personal data.
// Later: POST .../{onboardingId}/personal-data
//        POST .../economic-data
//        POST .../identity-documents
//        POST .../kyc
//        POST .../completion

A company is POST /api/v1/onboarding/businesses, then company data, beneficial owners, documents, authorized signers, business verification, and completion.

The panel is the OpenAPI file from exp-onboarding. Read the example before you open an operation. The spec schema for the start lists the required name and email. The family and the party id are read by the service when you send them.

docs.title: Profile
docs.text:
Ada reads who she is, and she reads the agreements she holds. Access is checked before either read. A denied caller gets nothing. The agreement list is not stored in the profile. Each row is fetched from the contract service, and the product name is fetched from the product on that agreement.

Her party id is 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111. Agreement 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000021 is in the list only when the contract service holds it for her. That is the Horizon Personal Loan the document prints. Source: the sandbox sample is 250,000.00 EUR. The profile returns the number, the status, and the product. It does not return the printed pages.

The service listens on port 8103.

// GET /api/v1/experience/profile/11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111
// Access must allow READ on PARTY. The body is her person record.

// GET /api/v1/experience/profile/11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111/contracts
// one item when the contract service has the sandbox agreement
{
  // contractId: 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000021
  // type: the contract number
  // status: the contract status
  // signedAt: when it was signed
  // productId: 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000202
  // productName: Horizon Personal Loan
  // productCode: the code on that product
}

A change of personal data is PATCH .../personal-data. If a later step of that change fails, the previous row is written back. Addresses, consents, and identity documents are the other paths on the same party.

Stewarded by the Firefly Software Foundation. dev@fireflysoftware.io

domain-lending-credit-scoring is the decision service for every journey, and it is also the scoring domain. It is listed with Lending.

docs.title: DecisionPort
docs.text:
DecisionPort is io.fireflysoftware.domain.lending.creditscoring.core.decision.DecisionPort. The HTTP adapter is POST /api/v1/decisions (DecisionController).

The response is APPROVE, REFER, or DECLINE, plus reasonCodes. journeyStep is ONBOARDING, LENDING_APPLICATION, INSURANCE_QUOTE, INSURANCE_BIND, or CLAIM.

The rules engine is Jafly's. JaflyRulesEngineAdapter calls org.fireflyframework.rules.core.dsl.evaluation.ASTRulesEvaluationEngine from org.fireflyframework:fireflyframework-rule-engine-core, BOM 26.10.20. The sample file is rulesets/openplatform-journey.yaml. An installer replaces that file, not the engine. The full pin is in Jafly is the foundation.

REFER is the outcome the sample ruleset returns when the score is missing or below MIN_CREDIT_SCORE. A decision with a significant effect on a person, or a decision outside delegated limits, still goes to a person with delegated authority. The engine does not remove that duty.

docs.title: What sits next to the port
docs.text:
SandboxCreditReportAdapter supplies the credit facts when the caller does not. It does not call the network. The older scoring saga in the same service still writes scoring cases to core-lending-credit-scoring. A stored score is not itself APPROVE, REFER, or DECLINE.

domain-data-credit-bureaus is not called by the sandbox adapter. See Data and external systems.

AccessPort is a different check. It is not in the published main of the experience modules or the security center. See Security and access and the quickstart.

docs.title: Contract
docs.text:
Stewarded by the Firefly Software Foundation. dev@fireflysoftware.io

A contract is the agreement: who is on it, which products, in which currency, and whether it amends or renews an earlier agreement.

docs.title: What it owns
docs.text:
• The contract header and its status history.
  • One or more product lines. contract.product_id is the primary line.
  • Currency as currency_code, a VARCHAR(3).
  • An optional predecessor. link_kind is AMENDMENT or RENEWAL.

docs.title: What it does not own
docs.text: It does not own the party, the product catalog, or the account. Party and product appear as identifiers. A contract does not link to itself.

docs.title: Ubiquitous language
docs.text:
Name in code Meaning contract_line A product on the agreement. More than one line is allowed. product_id The primary line. predecessor_contract_id The earlier contract this one amends or renews. link_kind AMENDMENT or RENEWAL. Status DRAFT, PENDING_APPROVAL, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, TERMINATED, EXPIRED, CANCELLED. Delete Only in DRAFT. A later status is a status change, not a hard delete.

Next: Journeys.

docs.title: Contract core
docs.text:
core-common-contract-mgmt is the system of record for the agreement, its lines, its status history, and its predecessor link.

currency_code is VARCHAR(3). Cross-context party and product identifiers are UUIDs.

docs.title: Contract domain
docs.text:
domain-common-contracts owns the saga: create, update, status change, and delete. Delete runs only when the contract is DRAFT. Compensation restores the previous status history. The service calls core-common-contract-mgmt and does not import that core's internals.

Next: Core.

docs.title: Contract journeys
docs.text:
Other journeys call the contract domain when they need an agreement. They do not call core-common-contract-mgmt directly.

Journey How it uses the contract exp-profile Reads contract summaries through domain-common-contracts. exp-lending Calls domain-common-contracts when a lending screen needs the agreement. exp-distributor Calls domain-common-contracts for distributor agreements. domain-banking-accounts Its build includes the contract SDK when an account is tied to an agreement. The account journey still enters through exp-accounts, which calls the account domain.

Next: Domain.

docs.title: Customer
docs.text:
Stewarded by the Firefly Software Foundation. dev@fireflysoftware.io

The customer domain is the party. A party is either a natural person or a legal entity. Ownership and the other relationships are edges on that party, not a separate customer database.

docs.title: What it owns
docs.text:
• The party, and the person or company record that specializes it.
  • Industry classification: a scheme and a code, with one primary classification.
  • Party attributes for facts that are not person columns.
  • Relationship edges: who owns, controls, parents, or is an officer of whom.
  • KYC and KYB cases for that party. The case is not a column on the person.

docs.title: What it does not own
docs.text:
It does not own the contract, the product, the account, or the decision. Those contexts store a party identifier. They do not join the party tables.

AccessPort is not part of this context. It lives in the security center. See Access and identity.

docs.title: Ubiquitous language
docs.text:
Name in code Meaning Party The customer. A person or a legal entity. NaturalPerson A person party. LegalEntity A company party. IndustryClassificationScheme ISIC, NACE, NAICS, SIC, CNAE, or OTHER. The scheme is stored. CNAE is one scheme, not the only activity code. Party attribute Employment, housing, loans, and debts. Not columns on the person. Occupation, monthly income Stay on the person. PartyRelationship A direct edge. Kinds are OWNERSHIP, CONTROL, PARENT, OFFICER. The source acts on the target. Owners, subsidiaries, ancestors Walks over direct edges. Ancestors and subsidiaries are not stored as a closure. Cycles and self-links are rejected. Ownership percentage Optional, from 0 to 100. Several owners do not need to sum to 100.

Party reads:

  • /api/v1/parties/{partyId}/owners
  • /api/v1/parties/{partyId}/subsidiaries
  • /api/v1/parties/{partyId}/ancestors

Next: Journeys.

docs.title: Customer core
docs.text: The core is the system of record. Another context stores the party's UUID, not a foreign key into these tables.

docs.title: Party aggregate
docs.text:
core-common-customer-mgmt owns Party, NaturalPerson, LegalEntity, industry classification, party attributes, and PartyRelationship.

Direct edges are stored. Ancestors and subsidiaries are a walk. A person can own a company. A company can own a company.

docs.title: KYC and KYB records
docs.text: core-common-kycb-mgmt owns KYC, KYB, and AML screening records for a party. The party identifier points at the customer core. It is not a shared table.

docs.title: Customer domain
docs.text: These services own the sagas. They call a core SDK. They do not import that core's internals.

docs.title: Party
docs.text: domain-customer-people creates, updates, and changes the status of a natural person or a legal entity. It also changes contacts and relationship edges. Compensation restores the previous relationship or status. It calls core-common-customer-mgmt.

docs.title: KYC and KYB
docs.text:
domain-customer-kyc-kyb opens and updates a KYC case for a person and a KYB case for a company, and attaches evidence. Create is compensated by a delete on the core. It calls core-common-kycb-mgmt. It does not own the party row.

Next: Core.

docs.title: Customer journeys
docs.text: Two experience services speak this domain. Neither one writes the party tables. Each step calls a port. The default adapter calls a domain service. A later process engine can implement that port. That engine is not running.

docs.title: Onboarding
docs.text:
exp-onboarding owns two journeys: a natural person and a legal entity.

Concern Port, default adapter Person or company, contacts, industry classification, attributes, relationships domain-customer-people KYC or KYB case domain-customer-kyc-kyb Message to the party domain-common-notifications

On main, this service does not call POST /api/v1/decisions and does not contain AccessPort. The decision service already accepts journeyStep ONBOARDING.

A company classification is a scheme plus a code. Occupation and monthly income stay on the person. Employment, housing, loans, and debts are party attributes.

docs.title: Profile
docs.text:
exp-profile is the signed-in customer. It reads and updates the person, contacts, documents, consents, and a summary of active contracts.

It calls domain-customer-people and domain-common-contracts. The contract summary is a read across the contract context. The profile does not open the contract database.

Next: Domain.

docs.title: Product
docs.text:
Stewarded by the Firefly Software Foundation. dev@fireflysoftware.io

The product domain is the catalog. Pricing is optional configuration on a product. It is not a second catalog and not a chain of separate fee, bundle, feature, and limit aggregates.

docs.title: What it owns
docs.text:
• The product and its status.
  • Optional pricing rows: amount, rate, and fee, when the product is a loan that has them.
  • Price calculation, commission, and eligibility, computed from that configuration.

docs.title: What it does not own
docs.text: It does not own the contract that sells the product, the party who buys it, or the decision that approves the application. A product without lending pricing rows is valid.

docs.title: Ubiquitous language
docs.text:
Name in code Meaning DRAFT, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, RETIRED Product status. ACTIVE is the offered product. Not hard-deleted ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, and RETIRED products stay in the catalog. Pricing row Optional product_configuration. Absent amount, rate, and fee rows are valid when the product is not a loan. Fees, bundles, features, limits Not separate saga steps. They are not their own aggregates in the catalog saga.

Next: Journeys.

docs.title: Product core
docs.text:
core-common-product-mgmt is the system of record for the product and its configuration, including optional pricing rows.

DRAFT and SUSPENDED exist. The catalog saga also uses ACTIVE and RETIRED. Offered, suspended, and retired products are not hard-deleted.

docs.title: Catalog saga
docs.text: domain-product-catalog registers a product and publishes, suspends, resumes, and retires it. Fees, bundles, features, and limits are not separate saga steps. It calls core-common-product-mgmt.

docs.title: Pricing configuration
docs.text: domain-product-pricing writes optional pricing rows on that product. Creating a row is compensated by deleting it. Amending a row restores the previous configuration. A product that is not a loan is valid when amount, rate, and fee rows are absent.

docs.title: Calculation
docs.text:
domain-core-pricing-engine calculates a price, a commission, and eligibility from product configuration. It does not own the product database.

Next: Core.

docs.title: Product journeys
docs.text:
Journeys that show a product call the product domain, not the product core.

Journey Port exp-lending domain-product-catalog, domain-product-pricing, and domain-core-pricing-engine exp-distributor domain-product-catalog and domain-product-pricing

Next: Domain.

docs.title: Experience
docs.text:
Stewarded by the Firefly Software Foundation. dev@fireflysoftware.io

A journey is what a person or an employee does. It is not a copy of a domain.

Accounts, cards, and lending stay separate. Payments are their own journey. They are not a step inside the account journey. Insurance is its own journey: quote, bind, service, and claim. The contracts that already have an OpenAPI file are under API.

docs.title: Banking
docs.text:
• Open and close an account
  • Cards
  • Lending
  • Finance terminal. An employee signs in, the terminal checks administer, and impersonation stores the employee id and the customer id.

docs.title: Shared and insurance
docs.text:
• Onboard a person or a company
  • Customer profile
  • Insurance. Quote, bind, and claim. The policy and underwriting domains do not have an endorse saga or a renew saga.
  • Insurance terminal. An employee signs in, the terminal checks administer, and impersonation stores the employee id and the customer id.

docs.title: Finance terminal
docs.text:
An employee works the records Ada opens, without using her journey. The finance terminal is that desk. The employee signs in, the terminal checks that they may administer the area, and a change that names a customer first checks that they may act for that customer. Both identities are stored before the record changes.

The employee in the sandbox is sample-employee, actor 33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333. Ada is still sample-journey, party 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111. She cannot sign in here. The terminal asks whether the caller may administer, and the sample customer does not have that grant. denied-actor cannot sign in either. An unknown name is refused before any list is returned.

When the employee signs in, the session returns that employee id and the provider sandbox. No identity-provider process is started. Listing accounts then checks administer on the account area. The sample account anchor is 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002. If administer is refused, the list is empty of records because the call stops.

Updating Ada's account is different from listing it. The employee sends her party id and a reason. The terminal checks administer on the account, then checks impersonate on her party. If impersonate is refused, the account is not changed. If it is allowed, the terminal stores an audit row with the employee id and Ada's party id, and only then updates the record. Close, a decision, and attaching a distributor follow the same impersonation when a customer is named.

The areas are accounts, cards, lending applications, mortgage agreements, supply-chain agreements, collateral cases, collection cases, provisioning cases, and AML cases. A decision applies only where that area has one. Asking to decide an account is refused, because an account has no decision on this desk. Asking to approve or reject a lending application is allowed. Removing a draft applies only where that area allows removal.

The same employee can set a configuration value and can read master lists. Those calls check administer on the anchor. They do not impersonate Ada, because they are not a change to her record. The sandbox lists are currencies and countries. Any other master type is refused. A missing value on a close, when the status key has not been set, refuses the close. The sandbox store is the default. When firefly.terminal.adapter is domain, configuration and reference data go through the domain SDKs for environment configuration and reference masters, not through an HTTP client written in the terminal. Ada cannot open this terminal. Sign-in as sample-journey is refused before any list is returned.

sample-journey and denied-actor do not receive a session.

An update without Ada's party id, or without a reason, is refused before the record changes. Impersonation denied stops the update. Administer denied stops the list, the open, the configuration write, and the master read.

A master type other than currency or country is refused. A close whose status has not been configured is refused.

With the domain adapter on, an account holder change is sent to the accounts domain, which writes the accounts core. The terminal does not write that core itself. Insurance money is not this desk. This desk does not post a payment.

The employee cannot change that policy until impersonation stores both ids. Ada cannot sign in on this desk.

Sign-in checks that the caller may administer. The sample policy anchor is 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000005. If administer is refused, the employee gets no session, or, on a later list, no records. An unknown name is refused before that check returns a person.

Updating a policy sends Ada's party id and a reason. The terminal checks administer on the policy, then impersonate on her party. A refused impersonation does not change the policy. An allowed one writes an audit row with the employee id and her party id, then updates the policy. Closing a policy uses the configured status, which for a policy is cancelled. A claim can be closed, and a claim can be denied. A quote can be withdrawn, and a quote can be declined. Asking the policy area for a decision is refused, because a policy has no decide step on this desk.

The employee can also list distributors, set a configuration value, and read currency and country masters. Those check administer and do not impersonate, because they are not a change to Ada's policy. The terminal does not call those two with its own HTTP client. The sandbox store remains the default until that property is set. Insurance still does not post the ledger. Any cash stays on the payments journey. Ada cannot open this terminal. Sign-in as sample-journey is refused.

With the domain adapter on, a policy update goes to the policies domain, a claim to the claims domain, and a quote to the underwriting domain. Those domains store the rows in their cores. They do not post money.

docs.title: Open and close an account
docs.text:
Ada Lovelace wants a place to hold money at the institution. Opening that place is its own sitting. It is not the card sitting, and it is not the loan sitting. The Horizon Personal Loan on agreement 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000021 stays that agreement. The account she opens is a new record, with its own agreement written as part of the opening.

She is sample-journey, party 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111. She asks for a savings account in EUR. The journey checks access as that sample customer before it writes anything. If she is not allowed to create an account, the domain is not called and she gets no account id.

When access allows it, the account domain writes the row in order. It creates an agreement, puts Ada on that agreement, creates the account, posts an opening entry on the ledger, and creates the main balance space. She sees an account id, the new agreement id, and the status completed. The account number, the type savings, the status active, and the currency EUR are what a later read of that account returns.

Closing is a separate call. Access must allow close on that account. The same account record is then marked closed. She does not call the contract journey herself. The agreement that was opened with the account is finished inside the account close.

She can also close a statement, set a withdrawal limit, and sweep money between two spaces of the same account. The accounts journey calls the accounts domain SDK for those three. It does not call the accounts core itself. The domain then calls the accounts core SDK, which stores the statement, the limit, and the sweep. The same journey stores a servicing mandate for her on the account, and it asks the payments domain SDK to run a standing order and to create a direct-debit mandate. The payments domain calls the payments core SDK, which stores those two and can read them back. The sample statement uses an opening balance and two lines. The sample limit and the sample sweep are separate amounts on that account. Source: the sandbox statement opens at 100.00 USD with lines 25.00 and -10.00. The withdrawal limit is 50.00 USD. The sweep is 15.00 USD. The standing order is 25.00 GBP. The direct-debit limit is 100.00 GBP.

There is a longer opening as well. She can start it, send proof of income, and name a funding source. The account itself is opened only after those waits. If a step after the open fails, the account that was just opened is closed. The direct open is the call that checks access and writes immediately. The published OpenAPI file lists the longer opening, the read, and the close. It does not list the direct open as its own operation, so the panel does not invent one.

docs.title: What she is refused
docs.text:
When access is not allowed, nothing is opened and nothing is closed. The ledger is not posted.

A currency that is not a three-letter code, or a missing party or product on the direct open, is rejected by the request before the domain runs. The sample she can send is party Ada, account type savings, and currency EUR.

If the open writes the agreement and the account and then a later part fails, the opening is undone: the account is closed and the opening ledger entry is reversed. She should not be left with a half-open account.

docs.title: Where the records go
docs.text: The account row and its spaces live in the accounts core. The opening entry is a ledger posting, not a note on the account. The agreement id she receives is a contract record created for this account. It is not agreement 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000021.

docs.title: Cards
docs.text:
Ada wants a card she can use on an account she already holds. Issuing that card is its own sitting. The card is tied to an account id, but opening the account is not this call, and moving money on the card is the payments sitting.

She is sample-journey, party 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111. The sample account resource used for access is 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002. She asks for a card on that account, with her name Ada Lovelace to emboss, and a card program. She can ask for a virtual card. The journey checks access as the sample customer before it stores a card. If she is not allowed to create a card, no card id is returned.

When access allows it, the cards domain stores the card. She sees a card id and the status completed. A later read can show a masked number, the card type, the status, and an expiry. Activate, block, and cancel are later calls. Each one checks access again. Activate and block update the card. Cancel closes it. A denial on any of those does not change the card.

There is also a longer issuance. She starts it, confirms the address where a physical card should go, and sets a PIN. The card is issued after those waits, and then activated. If she is only asking for a virtual card on the direct issue, she does not go through that address and PIN wait.

A credit card can carry a line and a statement. Those rows live with the credit-card records the cards domain can call. A debit card does not need that line. The payments journey, not this one, is what posts a card movement on the ledger.

docs.title: What she is refused
docs.text:
When access is not allowed, the card is not issued, not activated, not blocked, and not cancelled.

A request that omits the customer, the account, or the card program is rejected before the domain runs. The sample she can send names Ada, the sample account, and the program.

docs.title: Where the records go
docs.text: The card row is stored by the cards domain in the cards core. The account id on the card points at an account. It does not copy the account balance onto the card. Money still posts on the ledger, and only when a payment is confirmed.

docs.title: Insurance
docs.text:
A person asks for cover, accepts it, and later reports a loss. That is one sitting. It is not three products glued together, and it does not collect a premium. Insurance does not move money, and it does not certify IFRS 17 or Solvency II. Where a premium or a claim payment would leave the institution, the payments journey and the ledger own that movement. This journey stores the quote, the policy, and the claim.

Ada Lovelace is sample-journey, actor 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111. The sandbox agreement she can name on the policy is 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000021, the same agreement the Horizon Personal Loan document prints. Naming it records the identifier. It does not disburse that amount, and it does not post a ledger entry.

She asks for a motor quote. The journey checks access as the sample customer. If that check is not allowed, the quote stops and nothing is stored. It then asks for a decision. She does not send a credit score. The sandbox report supplies 640, which is below the sample threshold of 680, so the outcome is a referral. A referral does not stop her. The submission is stored as received.

She binds a policy and names that agreement, a product, the line of business, the currency, and the inception and expiry dates. The same access check and the same decision run again. If she omits her party id, the agreement id is used for the check. The policy is stored as bound, and binding it issues the letter through the document domain SDK.

She registers a claim against the policy: a loss date, a cause, and a description. The catalog default is notified. Reading, updating, or changing a status later does not ask for another decision. Withdrawing the quote, cancelling the policy, and closing the claim do not either.

Endorse and renew are not operations on this journey, and they are not operations on the policy domain. Reinsurance, reserving, and insurance financials are not in this sitting. Staff work is the insurance terminal.

docs.title: What she sees
docs.text: A quote comes back with an id, a reference, and status RECEIVED when she omits a status. A bind comes back BOUND. A claim comes back NOTIFIED. A referral does not change those statuses. She does not see a ledger entry, and she does not see the Horizon Personal Loan amount move. Naming agreement 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000021 only stores that identifier on the policy.

docs.title: Where the records go
docs.text: The quote is stored by the underwriting domain. The policy is stored by the policies domain. The claim is stored by the claims domain. Each of those cores keeps its own rows. None of them posts cash. A premium or a claim payment, if the institution pays it, is a payments journey and a ledger entry, not this sitting.

docs.title: What a refusal does
docs.text:
If access is not allowed, the call stops before the credit report and before any record is written.

A decision of decline, which the sample rules return when high risk is true, stops the quote, the bind, or the claim registration. The reason code is HIGH_RISK. Nothing is stored. A referral is not a refusal.

If the catalog has switched an operation off, the call answers HTTP 409 and says that operation is not enabled. In the file shipped here, quote, bind, claim, status, withdraw, cancel, and close are all enabled.

The journey does not lapse or expire a policy. Those closes exist on the policy domain. The status stored for a cancelled policy is CANCELLED.

docs.title: Lending
docs.text:
A borrower asks for credit, and later lives with the loan that was granted. Applying is one step. Servicing is what she can do after the loan exists: change the rate, close it, take a payment holiday or end one, and ask for the money to be paid out or for an installment to be paid. The product she names chooses which record is opened. A personal loan, a mortgage, asset finance, and supply-chain finance are not four different sittings. They are routes on this one journey. There is no separate experience for a syndicated loan.

Ada Lovelace is the sandbox customer, party 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111. The product on the sandbox agreement 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000021 is Horizon Personal Loan, product 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000202. In the lending catalog that product is a personal loan. She applies for it: the product, an amount, and a term in months. The printed agreement is five years, so the application that matches that document asks for that amount over 60 months. Source: the sandbox sample is 250,000.00 EUR.

The journey checks access as sample-journey before anything else. If she is not allowed to create an application, nothing is written.

It then reads the parameter journey.lending.min-credit-score and sends that number with the decision, under the name minCreditScore. In the sandbox that parameter is 680. She does not send a credit score. The decision service fills 640 from its own sandbox report when the score is omitted. 640 is below 680, so the sample rules refer her. A referral does not stop the application. High risk is a decline, and a decline does not open a record.

The catalog then chooses the domain from the product. Product ...202 is a personal loan, so the personal-loan domain opens the agreement. A mortgage product opens a mortgage. An asset-finance product opens asset finance, as a lease or as a rental. A supply-chain product opens that agreement. A product the catalog does not list uses the default route, which in the sandbox is loan origination. Creating that loan application also issues the contract document through the document domain SDK. The application row, when the route is origination, is stored by the origination domain in the origination core. The personal-loan agreement is stored by the personal-loan domain. The servicing case, once the loan exists, is stored by the loan-servicing domain. Cash, when a disbursement or an installment confirms, is a ledger posting. The sandbox payments adapter does not post that ledger.

docs.title: What she sees on the calendar
docs.text: GET /api/v1/experience/lending/loans/{id}/calendar returns one row per installment. She sees the installment number, the due date, the principal, the interest, and the remaining balance. She does not see a participant register. Restructuring and the end-of-day accrual are not this read. The OpenAPI spec includes the path as readAmortizationCalendar.

docs.title: After the loan exists
docs.text:
She can change the interest rate. She sends the old rate, the new rate, the date it takes effect, and a reason: an index adjustment, a renegotiation, a penalty, or a promotion. She can close the loan and say why. She can take a payment holiday, and she can end it. Those four calls stay on the loan. They do not try a payment.

Asking for the money to be paid out, or paying one installment, does try and then confirm, through the payments port, in the same call. The sandbox adapter is the default. It keeps the try until confirm, and it does not post the ledger and does not run a challenge for this internal movement. Set firefly.experience.payments.adapter to hub and the same try and confirm go through the domain payments SDK. That live adapter does not invent a code, and it does not accept the word sandbox as one.

If the loan is syndicated, she can read the facility. The response is the facility id, the loan id, the currency, the commitment amount, and the status. The participant register is not on that response. There is no exp-syndicated-loans. This journey only shows her the facility.

docs.title: The schedule, the cash, and the day
docs.text:
Once the loan exists, the servicing record keeps a schedule. Each installment stores its due date, the principal due, the interest due, and the balance that remains after that installment. The rate on that schedule is not one number for every loan. It is read from the product's pricing: the interest bracket that matches the product and the amount. A personal loan and a lease do not share a bracket. The sandbox price is the default. It reads that configuration and does not open a network connection. A live price is selected with firefly.lending.price.adapter=engine.

A repayment marks the earliest unpaid installment paid, with the payment date and the amount, and posts the cash on the ledger. The sandbox ledger is the default. firefly.lending.ledger.adapter=sdk posts through the ledger instead. If that posting fails, the installment is put back and the repayment record is removed. If the balance update fails after the cash has posted, that posting is reversed.

A restructure does not throw the old schedule away. The unpaid rows that are still current are marked superseded and stay on the same loan. New rows are stored on that same loan, priced again from the product. Paid rows are left as they are. If the restructure has to be undone, the previous rows can be made current again and the replacement rows removed.

At the end of a business day, interest is accrued once for each open loan that does not already have an interest accrual on that date. Those amounts are posted as one general-ledger journal for the date and the currency. A second run for the same date finds the journal that is already there and does not post another. The sandbox general ledger is the default. firefly.lending.accounting.adapter left unset keeps that sandbox. The live adapter asks accounting to store the journal.

docs.title: What a refusal does
docs.text:
When access is not allowed, the application is not created, the rate is not changed, the loan is not closed, and no payment is tried.

A decline stops before the personal-loan domain, the mortgage domain, asset finance, supply-chain finance, or origination. The sample decline is high risk.

A servicing operation the catalog has switched off answers HTTP 409 and does not call the loan. In the file shipped here, rate change, close, both holiday calls, disbursement, and installment payment are enabled.

Confirming a payment the sandbox does not know, or confirming an outbound try with the wrong code, does not complete the payment. On the live adapter, the word sandbox is rejected before confirm is sent.
