docs.title: Onboarding
docs.text:
Someone new becomes a customer, or a company does. The same service runs both. What happens next depends on the product family she names. Banking families are regulated: deposits, payments, lending, and cards. Insurance is not. A regulated start registers the person and opens identity checks. A non-regulated start opens a contract and leaves quote, bind, and claim to the insurance journey. A decline stops either path before that write.

Ada Lovelace can be the person who starts. If she sends her party id 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111, that id is the one sent to the decision. If she omits it, the tenant id is used for the decision. The sandbox agreement 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000021 is not created by this call. A non-regulated start asks the contract service for a new contract id and returns that id as the onboarding id.

The journey checks access as sample-journey, the sandbox customer. If that check is not allowed, nothing is registered and no contract is opened.

The decision runs next, for onboarding. She does not send a score. The sandbox report is 640, below 680, so the outcome is a referral. A referral continues. High risk is a decline, and a decline does not register her and does not open a contract.

If she sends product family INSURANCE, the catalog says the family is not regulated and the industry is insurance. The journey opens a contract for that industry and stops. The response phase is NON_REGULATED. There is no identity case and no welcome-and-wait.

If she omits the family, or she sends DEPOSITS, PAYMENTS, LENDING, or CARDS, the regulated path starts. For a person it registers her from her name and email, opens an identity case, and sends a welcome. It then waits. She submits personal data, economic data, and identity documents, asks for verification, and asks to complete. A company uses the business call and waits for company data, beneficial owners, documents, authorized signers, a business verification signal, and completion. Replaying the same email does not create a second person.

If a later step of the regulated path fails after she has been registered, the journey asks for her closure and cancels the identity case. If registration never produced a person, that closure is skipped. If a step inside registration fails after some of her records exist, those records are removed.

A family the catalog does not know does not open a contract and does not start verification.

docs.title: What she sees
docs.text:
On the insurance start she sees an onboarding id that is a new contract id, phase NON_REGULATED, and next step INSURANCE. She does not see a person id created by this call, and she does not see an identity case. Agreement 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000021 is not that new id.

On the deposit start she sees a person id, a phase that is waiting for personal data, and a welcome notification. She then sends personal data, economic data, and identity documents. After verification and completion she sees the journey move forward, and finishing onboarding issues the welcome document through the document domain SDK. The same email sent again does not create a second person.

docs.title: Where the records go
docs.text: A regulated registration writes the person in the customer core and the identity case in the verification core. A non-regulated start writes a contract in the contract core and stops. Neither path posts money. The Horizon Personal Loan document is a later reading copy, not this call.

docs.title: What a refusal does
docs.text:
When access is not allowed, the workflow does not start and no contract is opened.

A decline returns the decision failure and writes neither a person nor a contract. The sample decline is high risk, reason HIGH_RISK.

A malformed personal, economic, or document signal is HTTP 400. If the regulated start does not reach the first wait within 30 seconds, the call times out. If the workflow has already failed, been cancelled, or timed out, the start is refused instead of returning an empty person.

The published spec lists tenant, first name, last name, and email as required. The service also reads productFamily, partyId, and actorId when they are present. Omitting productFamily is the regulated path, not an error.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
Person: POST /api/v1/onboarding/individuals on port 8096.

// Insurance. Opens a contract. Does not start identity checks.
{
  // tenantId: required identifier
  // firstName: Ada
  // lastName: Lovelace
  // email: her email
  // partyId: 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111
  // productFamily: INSURANCE
}
// onboardingId is the new contract id
// currentPhase: NON_REGULATED
// nextStep: INSURANCE

// A deposit. Registers her and waits.
{
  // same name and email
  // productFamily: DEPOSITS
}

Later person calls, each with the onboarding id from the start:

Call What she sends POST .../personal-data Address and personal details POST .../economic-data Income and housing POST .../identity-documents The documents POST .../kyc The signal to verify GET .../kyc/status Whether the case is open POST .../completion The signal to finish

A company uses POST /api/v1/onboarding/businesses and then company data, beneficial owners, corporate documents, authorized signers, business verification, and completion.

The type names are InitiateOnboardingCommand and ProductFamily. The regulated families in the sandbox catalog are DEPOSITS, PAYMENTS, LENDING, and CARDS. INSURANCE is NON_REGULATED. The calls are also on the onboarding API.

docs.title: Payments
docs.text:
A customer asks the bank to move money the bank holds. That sitting is its own journey. It is not a step inside opening an account, and it is not how an insurance premium is collected. Insurance does not move money. The ledger does.

The book of record is core-banking-ledger. Until the caller confirms, the money is only reserved. Confirm writes the ledger entry. For a credit that has to leave the bank, the rail is asked only after that entry exists. For a card, the payment service provider is asked instead of the rail. For money that arrives, the credit is accepted once and then posted once.

Ada Lovelace is signed in as sample-journey. Her actor id is 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111. The movement names the sandbox agreement 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000021. In the published payment case the amount is the transfer, not the amount printed on the Horizon Personal Loan document. Source: the payment case is 25.00 EUR. The loan document prints 250,000.00 EUR.

docs.title: Sending the transfer out
docs.text:
She asks to send the case amount from account 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000011 to a beneficiary, IBAN DE89370400440532013000. The scheme is a domestic credit transfer. The header X-Firefly-Username is sample-journey. If she omits it, the sandbox still treats the caller as sample-journey. If the header is denied-actor, the journey returns HTTP 403 and does not reserve anything.

The try places a hold. The ledger records two legs and does not post them: a debit of her account and a credit of the outbound clearing account. No rail message is sent. Because this is an outbound transfer, a numeric challenge is created. In the sandbox, a stand-in for the SCA core makes a six-digit code. When the deployment is live, core-common-sca-mgmt creates the operation and the code. Either way, the delivery shipped with this service puts that code on the try response. It does not send SMS, push, or email. The word sandbox is not the code.

She confirms by sending the numeric code back. Confirm posts the held legs on the ledger, and only then asks the rail to send the credit. A second confirm does not post again and does not send the rail again.

If she cancels while the payment is only reserved, the hold is released, the challenge expires, and no rail message is sent. Cancelling a payment that is already posted does not unwind it.

A domestic credit and an international credit both use the rail. International is SWIFT. When the catalog contains SEPA credit transfer, the domestic rail kind is SEPA. A card payout uses the payment service provider, and it asks for the same kind of code because it leaves the bank. An international transfer configured onto a card route is rejected.

docs.title: Money she already holds
docs.text: An internal transfer, including a move between spaces of the same account, does not challenge her. The setting that would demand a code for an internal movement is not present, so no code is created. Try still reserves the legs. Confirm posts them: from her source account to the other account, or from one space of an account to another space of that same account. Nothing is sent to a rail or to a card scheme. A space movement has to name a space type the catalog knows. The published case uses SAVINGS.

docs.title: Money arriving
docs.text:
A third party can credit her account 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000012. A domestic credit that arrives on the rail is accepted once, matched by the third-party reference. Try asks the rail to accept the instruction, then holds a debit of the inbound clearing account and a credit of her account. She is not challenged. Confirm posts that hold. The same reference tried again returns the same payment and does not accept the instruction a second time. Confirming again does not post a second entry. A card credit follows the same once-only posting, and the provider that accepts it is the payment service provider, not the rail.

There is no separate international inbound scheme. An inbound domestic credit is the arrival the router registers.

docs.title: What she sees
docs.text: On try she sees HTTP 201, a payment id, and phase TRYING. An outbound transfer or a card payout also shows a challenge id and a numeric code. An internal transfer, a space move, and an inbound credit do not show a code. On confirm with that code she sees phase CONFIRMED and the ledger posting. On cancel of a reserved payment she sees phase CANCELLED and no posting. A second confirm of the same payment does not add a second posting. The word sandbox does not confirm.

docs.title: Where the money goes
docs.text: The book is core-banking-ledger. Try only holds. Confirm posts. An outbound credit debits her account 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000011 and credits the outbound clearing account, then the rail is asked. An inbound credit debits the inbound clearing account and credits her account 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000012. An internal transfer debits one account and credits the other. A space move debits one space and credits another space of the same account. Insurance does not use this posting.

docs.title: What a refusal does
docs.text:
denied-actor, or any caller the sandbox does not entitle, is HTTP 403. The ledger is not touched.

Confirming with the word sandbox, or with any other value that is not the numeric code, rejects the challenge. The reservation is released. There is no posting, and the rail is not called.

If the rail refuses the outbound message after the ledger has posted, that posting is reversed.

A missing amount, a currency that is not three letters or not in the masters, a missing party, agreement, or payment method, an amount over the configured limit, or an unknown space type stops the try before a hold. An inbound credit without a third-party reference is refused. A cancelled payment cannot be confirmed.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
There is no OpenAPI file for this journey. The calls are on POST /api/v1/payments.

// POST /api/v1/payments/tries
// header X-Firefly-Username: sample-journey
{
  // scheme: DOMESTIC_OUTBOUND, INTERNATIONAL_OUTBOUND, PSP_PAYOUT,
  //         INTERNAL_TRANSFER, SPACE_TRANSFER, RAIL_INBOUND, or PSP_INBOUND
  // idempotencyKey: string. An inbound credit uses thirdPartyReference instead.
  // amount: 25.00
  // currency: EUR
  // partyId: 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111
  // contractId: 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000021
  // sourceAccountId: 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000011
  // destinationAccountId: required for an internal transfer and for an inbound credit
  // sourceSpaceId, destinationSpaceId, spaceType: a move between spaces
  // paymentMethodId: identifier
  // externalAccountName, externalIban, externalBic: the beneficiary on an outbound credit
  // thirdPartyReference: required on an inbound credit
}
// 201
{
  // paymentId: identifier
  // challengeId: present on an outbound transfer or a card payout, absent on internal and on inbound
  // challengeValue: the numeric code, not the word sandbox
  // phase: TRYING
}

// POST /api/v1/payments/{paymentId}/confirmations
{ "response": "the numeric code" }
// phase CONFIRMED, and the posting is present

// POST /api/v1/payments/{paymentId}/cancellations
// phase CANCELLED while the payment was only reserved

The type names behind the calls are PaymentScheme, MovementRoute, and the ledger, rail, card, and challenge ports. firefly.payments.mode=live selects core-banking-ledger, library-rails, library-psps, and core-common-sca-mgmt. The default is sandbox.

docs.title: Profile
docs.text:
The signed-in person reads who she is and which agreements she holds. She can correct a name, a phone, an address, a consent, or an identity document. She cannot open an account here, and she cannot move money here. Contracts on the profile are a read from the contract service, then a read of the product named on each contract. The profile does not open the contract tables itself.

Ada Lovelace is sample-journey, party 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111. She asks for her profile, and she asks for her agreements. The sandbox agreement 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000021 appears in that list when the contract service holds it for her. The profile does not invent the row. When the row is there, she sees the contract id, the contract number, the status, when it was signed, and the product id, name, and code. The Horizon Personal Loan document is the reading copy of that agreement. The profile is the list.

Every read and every change checks access as sample-journey. She must be allowed to read, or to update, the party. If she is not, the person service and the contract service are not called.

A change of personal data reads the current row, writes the new one, and keeps the previous row aside. If a later step of that change fails, the previous row is written back.

docs.title: What she sees
docs.text: A profile read shows her name and the contact facts the person record holds. An agreements read, when the contract service has agreement 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000021 for her, shows that contract id, the contract number, the status, when it was signed, and the product id, name, and code. The product on the sample is the Horizon Personal Loan. The profile does not show the printed pages and does not show the amount. Those are on the document.

docs.title: Where the records go
docs.text: The person row is in the customer core. Each agreement row is in the contract core. The product name is read from the product catalog. The profile does not keep a copy of those tables. A corrected name is written back to the person row. Money is not posted here.

docs.title: What a refusal does
docs.text:
When access is not allowed, the call returns no profile and no agreements. An update is not attempted.

The check is made as sample-journey. In the sandbox policy that actor may read and update the sample party. A policy that does not grant her stops the call before either service.

A contract the contract service does not have for her is simply absent from the list. The profile does not answer with an empty product in its place. If the product named on a contract cannot be read, that agreement still comes back with the contract fields and without a product name.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
The service listens on port 8103. The party id is in the path.

What she does Call Read herself GET /api/v1/experience/profile/{partyId} Change personal data or contact data PATCH .../personal-data or .../contact-data Addresses GET, POST, PUT, DELETE .../addresses Consents GET .../consents and PUT .../consents/{id} Identity documents GET, POST, DELETE .../identity-documents Agreements GET /api/v1/experience/profile/{partyId}/contracts 
// GET /api/v1/experience/profile/11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111/contracts
// each item
{
  // contractId: 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000021 when that agreement is hers
  // type: the contract number
  // status: the contract status
  // signedAt: when it was signed
  // productId, productName, productCode: the product on that agreement
}

The JSON property for the contract number is type. The type names are ContractSummary and the party profile port. Full terms stay on the contract service. The calls are also on the profile API.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Stewarded by the Firefly Software Foundation. dev@fireflysoftware.io

OpenPlatform is a banking core and an insurance core. Products and the processes around them are built on those cores. A deposit account, a loan, and a policy are records in a core. The journey that opens them does not own the tables.

Insurance records policies, claims, premium schedules, and reserves. It does not move money and it does not certify IFRS 17 or Solvency II.

Each process is a port. The journey calls the port. The adapter that answers today is the domain saga: create, update, change status, and close, with compensation, through that context's core. A later process engine can implement the same port. The journey stays. A later payment rail, payment provider, or identity adapter is the same kind of replacement. The journey does not learn the new system.

Identity and the rules engine are Jafly, from Firefly Framework, org.fireflyframework, BOM 26.10.20. OpenPlatform does not fork them. The sandbox identity adapter does not start Keycloak. The sandbox credit report does not call a bureau.

A customer journey runs a product through its life. Origination starts it. Servicing continues it. Both live in exp-lending. Account and card tasks stay their own journeys, because a person does those as separate work. The finance staff terminal and the insurance staff terminal are the matching journeys for an employee: sign in, impersonate the customer, then run an operation on the same kind of record, and also run back-office work the customer does not run.

Layers inside a business domain

Experience

A journey. One service can call several domain sagas. It does not own the database.

Domain

The saga for one bounded context. Create, update, status, and close, with compensation.

Core

The system of record. Other contexts keep an identifier, not a foreign key into these tables.

Journeys are sequence diagrams under Experience. This picture is only the layer stack.

DecisionPort and SandboxCreditReportAdapter are in domain-lending-credit-scoring. POST /api/v1/decisions is the HTTP adapter. The rules engine is Jafly's, BOM 26.10.20. OpenPlatform does not ship a forked engine.

AccessPort runs before a journey changes a resource. A denial does not call the domain. The HTTP check is POST /api/v1/access/checks on domain-core-security-center.

The domain saga then writes one core through that core's SDK. It does not import another core's internals. Cross-service links are UUIDs. Child rows inside one core cascade on delete. Currency is VARCHAR(3).

docs.title: A process engine later
docs.text: An experience step calls a port. The default adapter calls a domain service. A later process engine can implement that same port. This version does not run that engine. No diagram here shows one in the call path.

docs.title: Keycloak is not a journey call
docs.text:
domain-core-security-center depends on org.fireflyframework:fireflyframework-security-idp-keycloak. That module is a Jafly identity-provider adapter, BOM 26.10.20. The journey does not construct a Keycloak client. The default is firefly.security-center.identity.adapter=sandbox. An installer sets keycloak, cognito, or internal-db. The decision call does not read that property.

Jafly (org.fireflyframework, BOM 26.10.20) is the identity and the rules engine, from Firefly Framework. OpenPlatform does not fork it. See Jafly.

docs.title: Open a layer
docs.text:
• Experience. The journeys, not a list of domains.
  • Domain. The saga rule and every domain-* service.
  • Core. Persistence rules and every core-* service.
  • Libraries. Payment ports, batch jobs, the parent, and the bill of materials.

The same repositories, grouped by business, are the families.

docs.title: ACORD alignment for OpenPlatform insurance
docs.text:
This file maps Firefly OpenPlatform insurance services onto the ACORD Capability Model. It is a mapping of services that exist in this workspace. It is not an ACORD assessment.

Insurance services do not move money. Where a capability collects or pays, the banking payments journey exp-payments and the ledger core-banking-ledger own the movement and the ledger entry. An insurance row may store an amount and a payment-order id aimed at core-banking-payments. That id is not a ledger posting.

docs.title: Source
docs.text:
Source: the public name is still the ACORD Capability Model, a facet of the ACORD Reference Architecture. Read on 20 October 2026 at https://www.acord.org/standards-architecture/reference-architecture. That page lists seven facets and shows ACORD Capability Model 2.6 as the current edition, with 2.5 and 2.4 still listed. The same page lists ACORD Information Model 2.13 and names the concepts Policy, Product, Party, and Claims.

Source: the 21 May 2025 ACORD note at https://www.acord.org/ACORD-about/acord-news/2025/05/21/acord-reference-architecture-updates-capability-model-business-glossary still calls it the ACORD Capability Model, describes ten high-level business capabilities, and names Business Management and Enterprise Services among them. It does not rename the model.

Source: the 29 January 2026 ACORD note at https://www.acord.org/ACORD-about/acord-news/2026/01/29/acord-releases-interactive-online-versions-of-reference-architecture-models keeps the same seven facets. It gives underwriting, policy administration, and digital marketing as examples of value-chain activities. The full Capability Model 2.6 decomposition is member access. This file does not treat "policy administration" as a new title. In the published model that activity is Contract Administration.

Source: second-level names below come from The ACORD Capability Model (ACORD Corporation, first printing October 2010) and from the ACORD 2011 framework slides that list the same ten top-level capabilities: Business Management, Channel Management, Claims, Contract Administration, Customer Service, Enterprise Services, Finance, Marketing, Product, and Sales. The May 2025 note still says there are ten. Where a 2.6 name was not on a public page, the row was left out.

This mapping uses that capability model and the Information Model names Policy, Product, Party, and Claims. It does not use IFRS 17, Solvency II, or the IAIS Insurance Core Principles.

docs.title: How a row is marked
docs.text:
A row exists only when the capability name is public and an insurance journey, domain, or core performs it, or when that named capability has no OpenPlatform service.

  • covers means an insurance service performs that capability.
  • partial means the service performs part of it and leaves out a material part.
  • absent means the capability is in the public model and OpenPlatform has no service that performs it.

No row is marked covers. Each named capability still includes work these services do not do, such as pricing, fraud detection, reserve calculation, or cash movement.

Groups follow the ACORD capabilities the insurance code can support: Channel Management, Sales, Contract Administration, Underwriting, Claims, Finance, and one Business Management activity. Underwriting is the shared capability the 2010 model places with Contract Administration process maps, and the January 2026 note lists it beside policy administration. Customer Service, Marketing, Product, and the rest of Business Management and Enterprise Services are not opened here. A Policy or submission stores a product id aimed at core-common-product-mgmt, which is outside these insurance repositories. Digital marketing appears only as an example on the January 2026 page, without a formal lower-level title on that page.

docs.title: Journey
docs.text:
exp-insurance is the insurance journey, at https://github.com/fireflysoftwaresolutions/exp-insurance. It calls domain-insurance-underwriting, domain-insurance-policies, and domain-insurance-claims. Reinsurance, reserving, and insurance financials are not on this journey. Staff administration is exp-insurance-terminal.

Quote, bind, and claim registration read a credit report and call domain-lending-credit-scoring. A decline stops before the insurance domain. Status, withdraw, cancel, and close do not take that decision.

Operations on the journey:

Operation Path Create, read, update, status, and withdraw a quote /api/v1/experience/insurance/quotes Bind, read, update, status, and cancel a policy /api/v1/experience/insurance/policies Register, read, update, status, and close a claim /api/v1/experience/insurance/claims

The quote is an underwriting submission. The catalog default is received for a quote, bound for a policy, and notified for a claim. Endorse and renew are not operations on this journey or on domain-insurance-policies. They are not mapped.

docs.title: Channel Management
docs.text:
Distribution in the model is Channel Management: channel development, channel strategy, producer management, channel execution, and channel planning.

ACORD capability Repository Layer Mark What is implemented Producer management exp-insurance-terminal journey partial The staff terminal lists distributors from core-common-distributor-mgmt and writes an attachment to that distributor's audit log, and core-insurance-underwriting can store a distributor id on a submission. Producer compensation core-insurance-financials core partial The financials core stores commission amounts with a payment-order id for core-banking-payments, domain-insurance-financials does not post commission, and exp-payments and core-banking-ledger own the payment and the ledger entry. Channel development none none absent No OpenPlatform service develops an insurance distribution channel. Channel strategy none none absent No OpenPlatform service sets insurance channel strategy. Channel planning none none absent No OpenPlatform service plans producer production. Producer Agreement Administration none none absent No OpenPlatform service administers a producer agreement, and binder records stay in the unmapped section below.

docs.title: Sales
docs.text:
Sales has one sub-capability in the published model, Contract Acquisition, whose execution process maps include Provide Quote and Apply for Insurance.

ACORD capability Repository Layer Mark What is implemented Sales Execution exp-insurance journey partial The journey creates, reads, updates, changes status, and withdraws an underwriting submission as the quote, and it leaves the priced quote record on core-insurance-underwriting unwritten.

docs.title: Contract Administration
docs.text:
The January 2026 note calls this part of the value chain policy administration. The capability name in the model is Contract Administration. Data names are Policy and Party.

ACORD capability Repository Layer Mark What is implemented Contract Lifecycle Management exp-insurance journey partial The journey binds, reads, updates, changes status, and cancels a Policy, domain-insurance-policies also lapses and expires it, and core-insurance-policies enforces quote, bound, in force, lapsed, canceled, and expired while storing coverages, Party roles, insured objects, a certificate, and motor, property, liability, life, and health detail. Contract Investment Administration none none absent No OpenPlatform service administers investments on a contract, and life detail stores a sum assured and a term.

The stored policy status for canceled is CANCELLED. A lapsed Policy can return to in force through the core status machine. The journey has no lapse or expire path of its own. Those two closes are on the policies domain.

docs.title: Underwriting
docs.text:
ACORD capability Repository Layer Mark What is implemented Underwriting core-insurance-underwriting core partial The underwriting core stores submission risk, evidence references, clearance, referral, decision, subjectivity, loss run, statement of value, a sanctions-screen result, and a priced quote, and it does not rate the risk or apply authority, while domain-insurance-underwriting moves submission status and the staff terminal can decline or withdraw by that status.

The journey's quote, quote status, and withdraw call that same submission status path. They are mapped under Sales Execution. The domain does not call the sanctions, referral, or decision APIs.

docs.title: Claims
docs.text:
The Information Model name is Claims. Second-tier names are Claims Lifecycle Management, Fraud Management, Claims Handling, Claims Recovery, Dispute Resolution, and Claims Inquiry.

ACORD capability Repository Layer Mark What is implemented Claims Lifecycle Management exp-insurance journey partial The journey registers a Claim, updates it, changes its status, and closes it, domain-insurance-claims and the staff terminal can deny one, and core-insurance-claims enforces notified, open, under assessment, reserved, settled, closed, reopened, and denied. Claims Inquiry exp-insurance journey partial The journey reads one Claim, and exp-insurance-terminal lists and opens claims, with no separate inquiry case. Fraud Management core-insurance-claims core partial The claims core stores fraud indicators and special-investigation referrals and does not detect fraud, and domain-insurance-claims does not call those operations. Claims Handling core-insurance-claims core partial The claims core stores coverage checks, triage, adjuster assignment, assessment, denial, evidence references, case reserves, and an authorized settlement with a payment-order id for core-banking-payments, the claims domain does not write those rows, and exp-payments and core-banking-ledger own any payment and the ledger entry. Claims Recovery core-insurance-claims core partial The claims core stores subrogation, salvage, and contribution amounts and does not collect them, and exp-payments and core-banking-ledger own any cash movement and the ledger entry. Dispute Resolution none none absent No OpenPlatform service manages litigation or another dispute on a claim. Catastrophe Planning none none absent No OpenPlatform service plans for a catastrophe or simulates loss projections.

docs.title: Finance
docs.text:
Finance in the model includes Billing and Payments, split into Billing and Collection and Payment Management, and the process map Analyze Reserves.

ACORD capability Repository Layer Mark What is implemented Billing and Collection core-insurance-financials core partial The financials core stores a premium schedule, installments, a premium audit, and a credit-control case, with each installment holding an amount and a payment-order id for core-banking-payments, domain-insurance-financials opens, cancels, and completes the schedule, and exp-payments and core-banking-ledger own collection and the ledger entry. Payment Management core-insurance-financials core partial The financials core stores premium refunds and indemnity disbursements as amounts plus a payment-order id for core-banking-payments, the financials domain does not pay them, and exp-payments and core-banking-ledger own the movement and the ledger entry. Analyze Reserves core-insurance-reserving core partial The reserving core stores a snapshot, loss-development triangle cells, and a reporting extract produced elsewhere and does not calculate reserves, and domain-insurance-reserving can mark the snapshot accepted. Investment Management none none absent No OpenPlatform service administers an insurer investment portfolio.

Case reserves on a single claim stay in Claims Handling. The reserving extract is stored input for Analyze Reserves. It is not a statutory filing.

docs.title: Business Management
docs.text: ACORD capability Repository Layer Mark What is implemented Perform Statutory Reporting none none absent No OpenPlatform service files a statutory insurance return, and a reserving extract is stored input only.

docs.title: Counts
docs.text: covers 0, partial 13, absent 9.

docs.title: Endorse and renew
docs.text: Endorse and renew are not mapped. exp-insurance has no endorse or renew operation, and domain-insurance-policies has no endorse or renew saga. core-insurance-policies can store a policy transaction whose type is ENDORSEMENT, RENEWAL, NEW_BUSINESS, CANCELLATION, or REINSTATEMENT. Creating that row does not move Policy status. Cancellation of a Policy is the journey cancel operation mapped under Contract Lifecycle Management.

docs.title: Insurance areas with no ACORD capability
docs.text:
These services exist on disk. The public Capability Model text read for this file does not name a capability they perform, so they have no row.

Reinsurance. core-insurance-reinsurance and domain-insurance-reinsurance store treaties and move them through draft, active, run-off, and expired. The core also stores policy cessions, with a ceded premium and a payment-order id, and claim recoveries. exp-payments and core-banking-ledger own any cash movement. The public names nearby are Manage Reinsurance Requirements, an Enterprise Services risk process, and Define Product Reinsurance Requirements, a product-design process. Neither is treaty, cession, or recovery administration.

docs.title: OpenPlatform mapped to the BIAN Service Landscape
docs.text:
This is a coverage map of Firefly OpenPlatform services that exist in this workspace onto the BIAN Service Landscape 14.0 Value Chain View. It is not a certification, a membership claim, or a statement of compliance.

BIAN groups service domains into business areas and business domains. A row appears only when that service domain is in the Value Chain View and its job is clear. A business domain is included only when at least one OpenPlatform journey, domain, or core performs one of its service domains. Business areas with no such service, including markets, treasury, corporate finance, trade finance, investment services, and corporate management, are left out.

Status meanings:

  • covers: the named service performs that service domain's job.
  • partial: the named service performs a slice of that job.
  • absent: BIAN defines the service domain, it sits in a business domain included below, and no journey, domain, or core performs it.

The repository column is the service that does the work. Gateways that only forward a call are not listed. core-payments-engine and core-common-pricing-mgmt contain no application code and are not treated as services. library-rails is a library, cited only where domain-payments calls it.

Channel Portfolio and Branch Portfolio are BIAN names in Channel management. The source extract used here has no job description for either name, so they have no row.

docs.title: Core
docs.text:
A core service owns its database. Another service does not share that schema.

Rules that hold across cores:

  • A link to a record in another service is a UUID.
  • Child rows inside the same service cascade when the parent row is deleted.
  • Currency is VARCHAR(3).
  • Accounts, cards, the ledger, and payments do not hard-delete an open record.
  • A contract is deleted only in DRAFT.
  • Offered, suspended, and retired products are not hard-deleted. DRAFT and SUSPENDED exist. Status values also include ACTIVE and RETIRED.

Ledger identification is initiating_party_identifier for the party that started the transaction and card_merchant_tax_id for a card merchant. Those columns are not NIF or CIF.

Where a core has no domain orchestrator, the catalog says so. In lending, that is core-lending-credit-cards. In banking, that is the ledger, payments, and open-banking access.

docs.title: Domain
docs.text:
A domain service owns one saga. The steps are create, update, status change, and close or remove. Close or remove runs only when the core allows it. Each write has compensation.

The domain calls a core through that core's SDK. It does not import another core's internals. Cross-service references that the core stores are UUIDs, not joined tables.

A few domain builds still declare an extra core SDK. That is a dependency, not permission to reach into the other core. The catalog entry names the extra SDK when the build has one: banking accounts (contract and ledger), banking cards (credit cards and ledger), and configuration (reference data).

Insurance domains follow the same saga shape. They do not move money and do not certify IFRS 17 or Solvency II.

Decision lives in domain-lending-credit-scoring. The credit-bureau and company-lookup ports live in domain-data-credit-bureaus and domain-data-business-intelligence. Those two own the port. They do not own a core database in this release list.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
Stewarded by the Firefly Software Foundation. dev@fireflysoftware.io

Three records sit under most journeys. Each has a core that owns the tables and a domain that owns the saga.

  • Party. Person or company, industry scheme, attributes, ownership graph.
  • Contract. Currency, product lines, predecessor, draft delete.
  • Product. Catalog status and optional pricing.

The decision call is a port on domain-lending-credit-scoring, not one of these tables. See Decision. Credit-bureau client code is a separate repository. See Data and external systems.

docs.title: Contract
docs.text: core-common-contract-mgmt owns the tables. domain-common-contracts owns the saga. Source commits: contract core 41d1f57, domain 5aec18b.

docs.title: Shape
docs.text:
currency_code is VARCHAR(3).

A contract has one or more contract_line rows when more than one product is on the agreement. contract.product_id is the primary line.

predecessor_contract_id points at an earlier contract. link_kind is AMENDMENT or RENEWAL. A contract does not link to itself.

docs.title: Status and delete
docs.text:
Status values used by the domain are DRAFT, PENDING_APPROVAL, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, TERMINATED, EXPIRED, and CANCELLED.

Delete runs only in DRAFT. A later status is a status change, with compensation that restores the previous history row, not a hard delete of an open contract.

The domain calls the contract core SDK and does not import that core's internals.

Catalog: Contract.

docs.title: Party
docs.text: core-common-customer-mgmt owns the tables. domain-customer-people owns the saga. Source commits on main: customer core 8cd2d6c, domain 62f5f8e.

docs.title: Records
docs.text:
A party is a NaturalPerson or a LegalEntity.

Industry classification is a scheme and a code. The scheme is one of ISIC, NACE, NAICS, SIC, CNAE, or OTHER. One classification is primary. The scheme is stored. It is not implied by the installation country. CNAE is one allowed scheme, not the only activity code.

Extra facts live in party attributes. Employment, housing, loans, and debts are attributes. They are not columns on the person. Occupation and monthly income stay on the person.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
PartyRelationship stores a direct edge. The source acts on the target. The kind is OWNERSHIP, CONTROL, PARENT, or OFFICER.

A person can own a company. A company can own a company. Ancestors and subsidiaries are a walk over those edges. The walk is not a stored closure. A cycle is rejected. A party cannot link to itself.

Ownership percentage is optional and is from 0 to 100 inclusive. Several owners do not need to sum to 100.

docs.title: Product
docs.text: core-common-product-mgmt owns the product tables. domain-product-catalog owns register, publish, suspend, resume, and retire. domain-product-pricing owns optional pricing rows on that product. Source commits: product core ff8f9d7, catalog domain a5a1be5, pricing domain afd2f51.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: DRAFT and SUSPENDED exist. The catalog saga also uses ACTIVE and RETIRED. Offered, suspended, and retired products are not hard-deleted. ACTIVE is the offered status.

docs.title: Pricing
docs.text:
A product without lending pricing rows is valid. A product that is not a loan succeeds when amount, rate, and fee rows are absent.

Fees, bundles, features, and limits are not separate saga steps. Pricing is optional product configuration. Creating a pricing row is compensated by deleting that row. Amending a row restores the previous configuration.

domain-core-pricing-engine calculates a price, a commission, and eligibility from that configuration. It does not own the product database.

Catalog: Product.

docs.title: Documents
docs.text:
When an agreement exists, someone still has to hand the customer a page she can keep. That page is not the agreement record itself. The agreement stays in the contract store. The document is a reading copy: who the parties are, which product it is, the amount, the term, and the lines on it. A letter and a welcome do the same job in a shorter layout. An amendment and a renewal are reading copies that name the agreement they follow.

The sandbox customer is Ada Lovelace. She is the account holder. The sandbox agreement is 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000021. The product on that agreement is Horizon Personal Loan. The term is five years, from November 1, 2026 through November 1, 2031. Source: the sandbox sample prints 250,000.00 EUR. It was issued on October 20, 2026, and its status on the sample is Issued. The agreement has two lines. The first line is the principal, and it is the primary line. The second line is credit protection, and it is not primary.

Five kinds of document can be issued. A contract is the long reading copy of the agreement. An amendment is the long copy of a change, and it names the predecessor agreement 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000020 and states what changed. On the sample, the change is that the term now ends on November 1, 2031. A renewal is the long copy that continues that same predecessor. A letter is the short confirmation. A welcome is the short note that onboarding is complete and that this agreement records the Horizon Personal Loan for Ada. Those are the only kinds. The catalog does not issue any other layout.

Issuing the contract starts with the catalog. The request asks for template contract, in English, for a lending product, and it says the product is regulated. The catalog row has to match those facts, and the template code on the row has to be contract. The page is then rendered. The kit stylesheet, document.css, is written into the HTML. It is not linked as a separate file the reader has to fetch. Fonts are inlined the same way. On screen, the contract is a stack of A4 sheets. The cover is one sheet. The contents are the next sheet. Each part after that is its own sheet: parties, product, amount, term, and the two contract lines. The back page is its own sheet. An amendment and a renewal use the same sheet split. A letter and a welcome are shorter, and they still use the same inlined kit stylesheet.

The stored result is HTML, media type text/html;charset=UTF-8. A later read returns the document id, the template code, that media type, and the HTML. The sample file for the contract is the rendered contract in the document module. This page does not paste it.

Three journeys ask the document domain SDK to issue a page. They do not render it themselves. Finishing onboarding issues welcome for Ada's new party. Creating the Horizon Personal Loan application issues contract for that application. Binding a policy issues letter for that policy. The SDK is the contracts domain client KitDocumentsApi.

docs.title: What she sees
docs.text: On the contract she sees a cover, then contents, then a sheet for the parties, the product Horizon Personal Loan, the amount, the five-year term, and the two lines. The first line is the principal and it is primary. The second line is credit protection and it is not. Her name is Ada Lovelace, her role is account holder, and the agreement id is 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000021. The status on the sample is Issued. The dates run from November 1, 2026 through November 1, 2031. An amendment also names predecessor 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000020 and the sentence that the term now ends on November 1, 2031. A letter and a welcome are shorter and still name her and that agreement.

docs.title: Where the page is stored
docs.text: The agreement itself stays in the contract core. This call stores HTML. The sandbox store is the default and does not open a network connection. firefly.documents.storage=core writes that HTML into the document core. The kit stylesheet is inside the file. It is not a separate download.

docs.title: What can go wrong
docs.text:
A template the catalog does not have, or a row that is not active, or a row whose language, product family, regulated flag, or template code does not match the request, fails before anything is stored. The caller is told that nothing was stored.

An amendment or a renewal that does not name the predecessor agreement fails before render. An amendment that does not state what changed fails the same way. A currency that is not three letters, a missing party name, a missing agreement, or a document with no lines fails before the catalog is asked to render.

If the render is empty, nothing is stored. If the store accepts an id and then fails, that id is removed, so a later read does not return a half-written document.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
The call is issue, then read.

// Issue the sandbox contract
{
  // templateCode: contract
  // language: en
  // productFamily: LENDING
  // regulated: true
  // party.id: 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111
  // party.givenName: Ada
  // party.name: Ada Lovelace
  // party.role: Account holder
  // contract.id: 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000021
  // contract.status: Issued
  // product.id: 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000202
  // product.name: Horizon Personal Loan
  // currency: EUR
  // amount: 250000.00
  // issuedOn: 2026-10-20
  // effectiveOn: 2026-11-01
  // endsOn: 2031-11-01
  // lines[0]: id ...221, role Principal, quantity 1, primary true
  // lines[1]: id ...222, role Credit protection, quantity 1, primary false
  // predecessorId: absent on a contract
}
// An amendment or a renewal sets predecessorId to
// 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000020
// An amendment also sets change to
// The term now ends on November 1, 2031.

The five catalog codes are contract, amendment, renewal, letter, and welcome. The type names behind the call are DocumentPort and IssueDocument. The default catalog reader, the FreeMarker render, and the sandbox store are the adapters an installer can replace. firefly.documents.storage=core writes the HTML into the document core. firefly.reference-data.catalog.adapter=core reads the catalog from reference data. The stylesheet file that is inlined is document.css. sheets.css is the screen rule that gives each part its own A4 sheet.
